text:
A: Hiya, hello. Are you there? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, hi, hello! Sorry, I didn't know if I had to press something. I'm Donna.
A: No, you're fine, it just connects. I'm Julie. I'm in Ossett, West Yorkshire, near Wakefield.
B: Oh, Yorkshire, lovely. I'm in Thornton Heath, so Croydon, South London. Erm, sorry, I'm a bit nervous, I've never done one of these video ones.
A: Don't worry, it's only three minutes. So what do you do?
B: I'm a senior care assistant, in a care home in Norbury. Older people, residential. I've been doing it years now. That's my tabard on the chair, actually, I've only just got in.
A: Oh, so you've come straight off a shift?
B: Twelve hours, yeah. My feet are killing me, honestly. But it's alright, I love the residents. The families ask for me by name a lot of the time, so, you know, that's nice.
A: That's a hard job, that. I don't know how people do it. I'm a regional operations manager for a builders' merchants, so I've got six branches across West and South Yorkshire. Completely different world.
B: Six! So you're the boss, then.
A: Well, sort of. I'm the one who gets the phone call when something goes wrong, put it that way. I've been there twenty-four years, started as an admin clerk, so I've worked my way up.
B: That's good though, innit, working your way up. That's what I keep saying at my place, I've been there longer than half of them and I'm still not team leader. They keep giving the good shifts to the agency lot.
A: Oh, don't get me started on being overlooked. It's always the same, isn't it. You do the work and somebody else gets the title.
B: Exactly! Exactly that.
A: So have you got family down there?
B: Yeah, my husband Clive, and my son Jordan's still at home, he's twenty, doing an apprenticeship. And my daughter's got a baby, so I'm a nan! That's her photo on the windowsill there, my granddaughter.
A: Oh, she's gorgeous. I'm not a grandma yet, thank God. Mine have both gone. Callum's in Leeds and Megan's at uni in Nottingham, so it's just me, Gary and the dog now.
B: Aw, does it feel quiet?
A: Erm, yeah, a bit, if I'm honest. The house is very tidy, put it that way.
B: I'd love a tidy house! Jordan leaves his work boots right in the hallway every single day, I nearly go flying.
A: You want to try a Labrador coming in off the canal path. Bella. Mud everywhere.
B: Oh no. Is your mum and dad still about?
A: My dad is, in Wakefield. He's not so good, to be honest. My sister sees more of him than I do. Work, you know.
B: Yeah, I know. My mum's seventy-eight, and with my job I see what happens, you know what I mean, so I worry about her all the time. I'm round there twice a week at least.
A: That's good of you. Erm, sorry, what were we, oh, have you got anything nice planned? Holidays or that?
B: I wish! Nothing booked. I did Tenerife with my sister a while back, all-inclusive, that was lovely.
A: Oh, we go to Tenerife all the time! Same hotel, four-star. We did Dubai last time for a change, mind.
B: Dubai! Look at you. I'd need about four drinks to get on that plane, I'm terrible with flying.
A: Oh, it's fine once you're up. Seven hours, a film, a gin and tonic, you're there.
